fitReason: Visitor-first, method-focused assistive-AI backup. The current group offers a formal visiting-student inquiry route, and a full recent technical paper verifies artificial neural-network learning for prosthetic intent decoding. This is a specialized bioengineering setting; CS project scope and required physiology background need discussion.

physicalEvidence.summary: The full 2025 TNSRE paper uses a four-layer neural network to map eight EMG inputs into virtual muscle activation, coupled to biophysical dynamics for seven-degree-of-freedom hand/wrist kinematic prediction. Offline, streamed-data and live online adaptation were evaluated using human EMG and camera-derived trajectories. Experiments occurred in August–September 2024 at MIT; the later publication is not a new experiment date. The paper explicitly leaves integration into actual prosthetic controllers and dexterity assessments to further work. This demonstrates a substantive learned method, not verified learned control of an actuated prosthesis. Other laboratory bionic hardware and biological neural interfaces must not fill that missing execution link.

shortVisit.summary: The current official Biomechatronics FAQ explicitly accepts domestic and international Visiting Students through MIT’s formal Visiting Student Program and directs CV inquiries to Senior Lab Administrator Lindsey Reynolds at a2biomech@media.mit.edu. Due to budget constraints, support must come through the visitor’s institution, fellowship or another program. The FAQ separately says the lab has no volunteer or internship program. This is an inquiry route, not eight-week admission, funding or summer 2027 availability.
